memory_update.text: KRT is the cleanest underfollowed US-listed small-cap candidate for the restaurant takeout/delivery/cold-beverage packaging node, with direct foodservice disposables, compostable product lines, custom branding, and logistics exposure.
GPK should remain in the universe as a mid-cap paperboard foodservice packaging/QSR exposure bridge, but later layers must quantify foodservice mix versus broader consumer-packaging cyclicality.
REYN is a weaker second-order candidate: it has Hefty Tableware and some foodservice/non-retail exposure, but restaurant revenue purity needs verification before it survives beyond Layer 1.

USFD is a distribution-gate candidate rather than a packaging manufacturer; it may matter because restaurant disposables adoption depends on national fulfillment, private-label SKUs, and supplier substitution.
PTVE/Pactiv Evergreen is no longer US-listed after the April 1, 2025 Novolex acquisition and should be treated as a private context anchor or comparable, not an investable public candidate.

Need a later pass for private/context anchors and supplier maps: Novolex/Pactiv, Dart/Solo, WinCup, World Centric, Eco-Products, Amhil, and restaurant distributors may reveal customer dependencies that public filings do not expose.

node: Takeout, delivery, cold beverage, and prepared-food packaging/disposables
summary: Expanded the underfollowed public-company universe for restaurant takeout, delivery, cold beverage, and prepared-food packaging/disposables. The highest-relevance public small/mid-cap discovery candidate is Karat Packaging (KRT), which is directly tied to disposable foodservice products, restaurant chains, distributors, custom printing, logistics, and compostable/BPI-certified alternatives. Graphic Packaging (GPK) is a larger but still sub-mega-cap reference/discovery bridge with direct cups, lids, carry-out cartons, trays, and QSR/foodservice exposure. Reynolds Consumer Products (REYN) is a weaker but plausible second-order candidate through Hefty disposable/compostable tableware and foodservice/non-retail channels. US Foods (USFD) is not a packaging manufacturer, but its Monogram disposables/private-label distribution makes it a national fulfillment gate for restaurants that may determine SKU adoption, compliance substitutes, and availability. Pactiv Evergreen would historically have been a top public reference name, but it was acquired by Novolex and delisted on April 1, 2025, so it is treated as a private/context anchor rather than a candidate.
